decisions.reason: The equation used an undeclared U and an arbitrary continuous path, without an equation time range or differentiability condition. These are missing typing/domain conditions, not a quadrature-estimate failure. Declared U an open real interval containing [0,T], required the path restricted to [0,T] to be C1 for this equation, specified 0<=t<=T and domain-relative endpoint derivatives. The unchanged integral is well-defined because every shifted component times continuous K is continuous on [0,tau].

F4 incorrectly cited the retarded-equation definition, which has no grid. The Euler algorithm explicitly sets h=tau/m and uses nodes jh, so ktau=(km)h gives the claimed alignment. Corrected that citation to the already-declared algorithm dependency. This is nonfatal because the Statement itself already assumes the grid and alignment, and the interpolation proof follows from those hypotheses independently of F4’s former attribution.

Step 3.1 claimed the split lemma applied with a global E_h=h^2/4 although only [-tau,0] was controlled. That invocation is unsupported. It is nonfatal to the example’s numerical conclusions because steps 1.1 and 2.1 already compute the exact quadrature and node-history contributions and the total error independently. Replaced the invocation by the direct finite-sum bound: every sampled -theta_j lies in [-tau,0], so the node difference is at most Delta*r*h^2/4=tau*h^2/4. F3 now explicitly states its global-bound hypothesis and serves only as comparison of the two error terms.

reviews.reason: Checked the shift maps [0,tau] into [-tau,T] for every t in [0,T], componentwise continuity and Riemann integrability against the actual local supplier statements. The repaired equation has a defined field value and derivative at every declared time, using one-sided endpoint derivatives. No Lipschitz, existence or uniqueness claim is introduced; the history integral interface is preserved.

Checked convex nodal interpolation gives E, cellwise C2 permits integral Taylor remainders bounded by M times distance squared/2, and cancellation of the linear terms gives M h^2 lambda(1-lambda)/2<=Mh^2/8. One-sided derivatives suffice at cell endpoints; M=0 and E=0 are included. Corrected F4 to the actual Euler mesh supplier; the Statement is byte-for-byte unchanged. Focused precheck: one proof checked, zero failures.

Integrated each centered quadratic cell to obtain I-Q_ex=tau*Delta^2/12. The initialized-history chord error is v(h-v), has maximum h^2/4 and integral h^3/6; the q subcells lie within one affine chord, so their midpoint sum integrates it exactly. Thus Q_st-I=tau*h^2/6 and Q_st-Q_ex=tau*h^2/6+tau*Delta^2/12. The revised direct node-sum bound is valid on the queried negative-time window alone, for all m,q>=1 including m=q=1; no positive-time error assumption or global lemma application is made. The Example section is unchanged.
